J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 1.6.2016 at about 9.00 p.m. the petitioner was playing infront of her house at 3rd cross, T.K. Road, Kalanagar, Channapatna Town, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 had taken the car in a reverse direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner.
Consequent to the terrific impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Channapatna, wherein she took the first aid treatment, thereafter she was shifted to NIMHANS and then he was referred to Victoria hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
3.

Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy,
aged about 4 years, student.
On account of the injuries she could not attend the class.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, she prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsel, inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement, so the written statement of respondent No.1 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.2 has filed its respective written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 and its validity.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the Kumari Poonam vs Shri Gajendra C.V on 4 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147021359/
2 parents of the minor petitioner and they leave minor girl in the public place without taking any responsible and caution and abruptly left the minor child alone in the main road and she is suddenly cross because of their own negligence she sustained injuries and she is solely responsible for the accident.

As per the complaint, car bearing No.KA-52-C-8214 is involved in the accident and as per FIR registered against the car bearing No.KA-52-C-8214, but during the course of investigation learnt that said car is not having valid insurance and the vehicle records the owner of the car and the petitioner in collusion with the police falsely implanted the Nissan Sunny car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214.
Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.
6.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 on 1.6.2016 at about 9.00 a.m. near T.K.Kalanagara, 3rd cross, Channapatna Town, Ramanagara District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

8.

To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1.
9.
Heard the arguments.

Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved her case as contended in the petition by producing oral and Kumari Poonam vs Shri Gajendra C.V on 4 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147021359/

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the parents of the petitioner as they leave minor girl in the public place without taking any responsible and caution and abruptly left the minor child alone in the main road and she suddenly cross because of their negligence and caused the accident.
Further argued that Nissan Sunny car bearing NO.KA-51- C-8214 is not at all involved in the accident.

As per the complaint, car bearing NO.KA-52-C-8214 is involved in the accident and as per FIR registered against the car bearing No.KA-52-C-8214, but during the course of investigation learnt that said car is not having valid insurance and the vehicle records the owner of the car and the petitioner in collusion with the police falsely implanted the Nissan Sunny car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
13.
On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

To substantiate the said contention he has produced prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR with Complaint, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, certified copy of order sheet in CC No.1016/2016 of Ramanagara District, Acquisition CC No.1016/2016 respectively.
15.
On perusal of complaint marked at Ex.P1 reveals that, complaint has been lodged by the father of the petitioner G.Guruswamy on 6.6.2016.
Based on the complaint FIR marked at Ex.P1 has been registered against the driver of the car in Cr.No.81/2016 by Channapatna East police for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P2 is the Wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, Ex.P3 is IMV report also reveals the damages caused to the vehicle and IMV inspector has opined that accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

On perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P4 reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle driver for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the parents of the petitioner as they leave minor girl in the public place without taking any responsible and caution and abruptly left the minor child alone in the main road and she suddenly crossed because of their negligence and caused the accident.

To substantiate the said fact,
he has examined legal manager of respondent No.2-Insurance Company as RW1, he has reiterated the similar facts as stated in the written statement.

On perusal of complaint and FIR the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-52-C- 8214, but on perusal of IMV report and charge sheet the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-51-C-8214.
17.

18. On perusal of citation it is observed that, 'no material on record to show that wrong number of vehicle was noted by investigating officer, mere surmises and conjectures, no conclusion can be arrived at that investigating officer inadvertently mentioned wrong number of vehicle.
19.
On going through the Ex.P6 the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 has admitted the accident in a criminal court before the Addl. JMFC, Channapatna.
If the vehicle bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 has not involved in the accident the respondent No.1 would have challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214.
But the reasons best known to him he has not do so.
From this it is clear that he has admitted the accident.
20. The petitioner has examined I.O. as PW3.
He has stated in his evidence that the accident caused on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214.
Though, the respondent No.2 has cross-examined the PW3, but nothing worth material has been elicited from him.

21. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and PW3 and the documents placed before the court I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved her case that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-51-C-8214.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.

23. ISSUE NO.2:- PW1 being the father of the petitioner has stated in his evidence that petitioner has met with an accident on 1.6.2016 at about 9.00 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was taken to Channapatna Government hospital, wherein she took treatment inpatient, later on she was shifted to NIMHANS and then she was referred to Victoria hospital and admitted as inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, PW1 has produced wound certificate at Ex.P2,
which reveals the following injuries;
Left parietal scalp skin opened with skull exposed 24.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury is grievous in nature.
25. PW2-Dr.Ramesh has stated that the petitioner has sustained scalp avulsion injury and underwent wound debridement and suturing done.
He has produced Ex.P11 and Ex.P12 such as OPD Book and case sheet.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for Kumari Poonam vs Shri Gajendra C.V on 4 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147021359/
5 which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: 26. The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 4 years.
Due to the accidental injuries she has suffered a lot.
PW1 has produced Ex.P9 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 1.6.2016 and discharged on 9.6.2016.
During the said period either father or mother, one has to look after their daughter by leaving their work.
So, I deem it fit to grant Rs.20,000/- under the head of inconvenience caused to the parents during the treatment period.
Therefore, Rs.20,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
27. The contention of PW1 is that, they have spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

He has produced the medical bills at Ex.P8 to the extent of Rs.12,503/- supported with prescriptions,
hence, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.12,503/- under the head of medical expenses.

28. Further contention of the PW1 is that, prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 4 years, student.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has became permanent disability as she is getting headache, giddiness and do normal activities.
29 PW2-Dr.Ramesha K.T. has stated in his evidence that he has examined the petitioner on 4.4.2019 for disability assessment.
He has assessed the facial disability at 6.25%.

He has been cross-examined by the respondent No.2 and admitted that he has not mentioned in his chief-examination as per Gazette notification the injuries of the petitioner comes under the category of disability.
Therefore, no amount is granted for disability.
30. PW1 has stated that due to the accidental injuries petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced the photographs, which are not marked, which shows that the petitioner has sustained injury on her head and forehead.
Therefore, Rs.50,000/- is granted for disfiguration.
31. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident petitioner took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient.
On perusal of Ex.P9 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 1.6.2016 and discharged on 9.6.2016.
So, one must attend her during the above said period.

So, considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,000/-under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
32.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No.
Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 30,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 20,000-00 and rest period

3. Medical expenses Rs. 12,503-00 4. Disfiguration Rs. 50,000-00 Kumari Poonam vs Shri Gajendra C.V on 4 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147021359/
6 5. Loss of amenities, Attendant, Rs. 20,000-00
Nourishment and conveyance charges Total Rs.1,32,503-00 33.
LIABILITY:

As I have already discussed in issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214.
34.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of car bearing No. KA-51-C-8214 and its validity.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,32,503/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/schedule bank till she attains age of majority and after attaining the age of majority the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
